newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Negligence cited in Pakistani rail crash.
newsitem.headline: Negligence cited in Pakistani rail crash.

text.p: An inquiry into a train crash that killed 128 people and wounded 60 in Pakistan this month has blamed negligence by railway employees for the tragedy, a government official said on Monday.

The official said a committee set up by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif to investigate the March 3 crash in the central province of Punjab pinned the blame on the staff at Khanewal station, the driver, and a train guard.
"The accident was caused by gross negligence of railway employees," said the official, who asked not to be named. "The disaster could have been averted."
Newspapers quoted committee chairman Sikander Hayat as saying: "The train was not fit for operation, but was allowed to leave after it was declared fit for operation."
Hayat said the team would soon submit its findings to Sharif with recommendations for improving state-run Pakistan Railways.
Controllers had switched the train to a dead-end line to prevent it from hitting an oncoming Karachi-Lahore express train on the single-track line.
But the diverted train slammed into the buffers at the end of the spur line near the village of Mir Shah, about five km (three miles) from Khanewal, derailing the engine and five coaches.
The inquiry committee found there was no need to divert the train because the Karachi-Lahore express had been delayed.
The report said the guard at the back of the train could not warn the driver at the front that the brakes had failed because there was no proper communication link between them.
The inquiry ruled out sabotage or terrorism as possible causes of the accident.
The federal government's inspector of railways, Muhammad Afzal Khan, said he was preparing a report on the accident and would submit it to the government next week.
